title: Refuse bee backlog add by naming the real problem
action: Make `bee backlog add` refuse honestly instead of emitting the router's generic `unsupported_argument_shape`. Reproduce first: `bee backlog add --json --title smoketitle` today answers "unsupported argument shape ... Its required arguments are all present, so what it refused is an optional flag, a flag value, or a target that does not exist" - which is false; what it refused was the MISSING --type. Root cause, in `fn run_add` (find it with `rg -n 'fn run_add' packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/backlog.rs`): every validation miss returns `None`, the old "delegate to Node" signal, and Node was deleted, so `try_native` falls through to the router's generic shape diagnosis in `packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/router.rs` (`rg -n 'unsupported_argument_shape' packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/router.rs`). The decisive lines in run_add: `let ty = require_flag(&parsed, "type")?;`, `if !backlog_allowed_type(ty) { return None; }`, `let title = require_flag(&parsed, "title")?;`, `let severity = require_flag(&parsed, "severity")?;`, `if !BACKLOG_SEVERITIES.contains(&severity) { return None; }`, `let layer = require_flag(&parsed, "layer")?;`, `if char_len(title) > BACKLOG_MAX_TITLE || char_len(layer) > BACKLOG_MAX_LAYER { return None; }`, and the append failure `if append_jsonl(...).is_err() { return None; }`. Replace each with a typed refusal that names the actual problem and the fix, reusing the emit shape run_add ALREADY uses for --queue-submit a few lines below (`return Some(emit_error(&ctx.root, "backlog add", parsed.json, &msg, t0));`). Two constraints follow from that: emit_error needs the root, so the `preamble` call must move ABOVE the validation block - keep its existing Err/Ok(None) handling byte-identical, and keep the no-root and unsupported-root paths winning over a validation message, since a caller outside a bee repo must still hear about the root first. Message content, one per problem: a missing --type/--title/--severity/--layer names which flag is missing and that all four are required; an out-of-enum --type names the value and points at `bee backlog add --help`; an out-of-enum --severity names the value and lists P1|P2|P3; an over-length --title or --layer names which one, its length and the limit. Every refusal must leave .bee/backlog.jsonl untouched, as the help text already promises. Do NOT change the success path, the row key order, the --queue-submit refusal, or any other verb in this file. Tests in the file's own #[cfg(test)] block if it has one, otherwise in the crate's existing CLI-surface test file (find where sibling verbs are tested with `rg -rn 'backlog add' packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src --glob '*.rs'`): cover a missing --type, an out-of-enum --severity, an over-length --title, and one full valid call that still appends exactly one row - each asserting the refusal text names the real problem and that no row was written.

truths: A bee backlog add call missing --type names --type, never a generic argument-shape message
